questions.title: Create Hash From Pairs
questions.description:
Read N key-value pairs (one pair per line, separated by a space) into a hash and print all the keys separated by single spaces in insertion order.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Next N lines: a key and a value separated by a space.

Output Format:
One line of N space-separated keys.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= key length <= 20, 1 <= value length <= 20.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
h = {}
n.times do
  k, v = gets.split
  h[k] = v
end
puts h.keys.join(" ")

questions.title: Merge Inventory Counts
questions.description:
Two branch stores report stock counts per product. Combine them by summing quantities for matching products and keeping products only present in one store as-is. Print the combined totals sorted alphabetically by product. Implement the combination manually with each; the merge, merge! and update methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N1 (number of products in store 1).
Next N1 lines: product name and integer quantity.
Next line: integer N2 (number of products in store 2).
Next N2 lines: product name and integer quantity.

Output Format:
One line per unique product (sorted alphabetically): '<product> <total_qty>'.

Constraints:
1 <= N1, N2 <= 100, 1 <= product length <= 20, 0 <= quantity <= 10000.
questions.sourcecode:
def combine_stores(store1, store2)
  totals = {}
  store1.each { |product, qty| totals[product] = qty }
  store2.each do |product, qty|
    if totals.key?(product)
      totals[product] += qty
    else
      totals[product] = qty
    end
  end
  totals
end

n1 = gets.to_i
store1 = {}
n1.times do
  p, q = gets.split
  store1[p] = q.to_i
end

n2 = gets.to_i
store2 = {}
n2.times do
  p, q = gets.split
  store2[p] = q.to_i
end

combined = combine_stores(store1, store2)
combined.keys.sort.each do |p|
  puts "#{p} #{combined[p]}"
end

questions.title: Sort Hash by Value Descending
questions.description:
Given a hash of products and sales counts, print them sorted by sales count descending, breaking ties by product name ascending. Implement sorting with a while loop (bubble sort). The sort, sort_by, max and min methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Next N lines: product name and integer sales count separated by a space.

Output Format:
N lines, each '<product> <sales>' ordered by sales descending (ties by product ascending).

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, 1 <= product length <= 20, 0 <= sales <= 10000.
questions.sourcecode:
def rank_by_value(pairs)
  n = pairs.length
  swapped = true
  while swapped
    swapped = false
    (n - 1).times do |i|
      a, b = pairs[i], pairs[i + 1]
      should_swap = false
      if a[1] < b[1]
        should_swap = true
      elsif a[1] == b[1] && a[0] > b[0]
        should_swap = true
      end
      if should_swap
        pairs[i], pairs[i + 1] = pairs[i + 1], pairs[i]
        swapped = true
      end
    end
  end
  pairs
end

n = gets.to_i
pairs = []
n.times do
  p, v = gets.split
  pairs << [p, v.to_i]
end

ranked = rank_by_value(pairs)
ranked.each do |p, v|
  puts "#{p} #{v}"
end

questions.title: Invert Hash Pairs
questions.description:
Given a hash where every value is unique, swap keys and values so each value becomes the new key. Print the inverted pairs sorted by new key. Implement inversion manually with each; the invert and transform_values methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Next N lines: a key and a value separated by a space (all values are distinct).

Output Format:
N lines, each '<value> <key>' sorted by value ascending.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= key length <= 20, 1 <= value length <= 20, all values distinct.

4
k1 v1
k2 v2
k3 v3
k4 v4

v2 k2
v3 k3
v4 k4

def flip_pairs(pairs)
  result = {}
  pairs.each do |k, v|
    result[v] = k
  end
  result
end

n = gets.to_i
pairs = []
n.times do
  k, v = gets.split
  pairs << [k, v]
end

flipped = flip_pairs(pairs)
flipped.keys.sort.each do |k|
  puts "#{k} #{flipped[k]}"
end

questions.description:
Given a hash of items with integer quantities, keep only entries whose quantity is strictly greater than a threshold. Print remaining entries sorted by key. Implement filtering manually with each; the select, filter, reject and keep_if methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Next N lines: item name and integer quantity separated by a space.
Last line: integer threshold.

Output Format:
One line per remaining item (sorted alphabetically): '<item> <qty>'.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= item length <= 20, 0 <= quantity <= 10000.

def keep_above(pairs, threshold)
  result = {}
  pairs.each do |k, v|
    result[k] = v if v > threshold
  end
  result
end

n = gets.to_i
pairs = []

  k, v = gets.split
  pairs << [k, v.to_i]
end
threshold = gets.to_i

kept = keep_above(pairs, threshold)
kept.keys.sort.each do |k|
  puts "#{k} #{kept[k]}"
end

questions.title: Nested Hash Student Average
questions.description:
Each of N students has M subject scores stored as a nested hash {student => {subject => score}}. Compute each student's average score across all M subjects and print 'student average' (2 decimal places) sorted by student name. Compute totals with each; the sum, reduce, inject, average and mean helpers are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: two integers N (number of students) and M (subjects per student).
For each student:
  Line 1: student name.
  Next M lines: subject name and integer score separated by a space.

Output Format:
N lines, each '<student> <avg>' (avg to 2 decimal places), sorted alphabetically by student name.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, 1 <= M <= 10, 0 <= score <= 100, 1 <= name length <= 20.

def student_score_rollups(records, m)
  result = {}
  records.each do |student, scores|
    total = 0
    scores.each do |_, score|
      total += score
    end
    result[student] = total.to_f / m
  end
  result
end

n, m = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
records = {}
n.times do
  student = gets.chomp
  scores = {}
  m.times do
    subj, sc = gets.split
    scores[subj] = sc.to_i
  end
  records[student] = scores
end

rollups = student_score_rollups(records, m)
rollups.keys.sort.each do |s|
  puts "#{s} #{'%.2f' % rollups[s]}"
end

questions.title: Cart Subtotal Calculator
questions.description:
A shop has a price list (item name -> unit price). A cart contains items with quantities. Compute the subtotal by multiplying each cart item's quantity by its unit price (skipping any cart item not present in the price list). Iterate the cart with each. The sum, reduce, inject, select and merge methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer P (number of priced items).
Next P lines: item name and integer unit price separated by a space.
Next line: integer C (number of cart items).
Next C lines: item name and integer quantity separated by a space.

Output Format:
A single integer: the subtotal (price * qty summed across matched cart items).

Constraints:
1 <= P, C <= 1000, 1 <= item length <= 20, 1 <= price <= 10000, 1 <= quantity <= 100.

4
pen 5
pencil 10
eraser 3
book 7
3
pen 2
book 1
eraser 4
questions.sourcecode:
def compute_subtotal(prices, cart)
  total = 0
  cart.each do |item, qty|
    if prices.key?(item)
      total += prices[item] * qty
    end
  end
  total
end

p_count = gets.to_i
prices = {}
p_count.times do
  item, pr = gets.split
  prices[item] = pr.to_i
end

c_count = gets.to_i
cart = {}
c_count.times do
  item, qty = gets.split
  cart[item] = qty.to_i
end

puts compute_subtotal(prices, cart)

questions.title: Default Value Counter
questions.description:
Read N space-separated words. Use Hash.new(0) to count occurrences of each word, then print each unique word with its count sorted alphabetically by word. Sorting must be implemented manually with a while loop. The group_by, tally, count and sort methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated words.

Output Format:
One line per unique word (sorted alphabetically): '<word> <count>'.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= each word length <= 20.
questions.sampleinput1:
6
apple banana apple cherry banana apple
questions.sourcecode:
def build_freq(words)
  freq = Hash.new(0)
  words.each { |w| freq[w] += 1 }
  freq
end

n = gets.to_i
words = gets.split
freq = build_freq(words)
keys = freq.keys.to_a
len = keys.length
swapped = true
while swapped
  swapped = false
  (len - 1).times do |i|
    if keys[i] > keys[i + 1]
      keys[i], keys[i + 1] = keys[i + 1], keys[i]
      swapped = true
    end
  end
end
keys.each do |k|
  puts "#{k} #{freq[k]}"
end

questions.title: Inventory Value Report
questions.description:
Read N categories, each containing M items with quantities. The data is stored as a nested hash {category => {item => qty}}. For each category, compute the total quantity across its items using each, and print 'category total' sorted by category name. The sum, reduce, inject, group_by and select methods are disabled.

Input Format:
Line 1: two integers N (number of categories) and M (items per category).
For each category:
  Line 1: category name.
  Next M lines: item name and integer quantity separated by a space.

Output Format:
N lines, each '<category> <total>' sorted alphabetically by category name.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, 1 <= M <= 100, 1 <= name length <= 20, 0 <= quantity <= 10000.

def category_totals(records)
  result = {}
  records.each do |cat, items|
    total = 0
    items.each do |_, qty|
      total += qty
    end
    result[cat] = total
  end
  result
end

n, m = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
records = {}
n.times do
  cat = gets.chomp
  items = {}
  m.times do
    name, qty = gets.split
    items[name] = qty.to_i
  end
  records[cat] = items
end

totals = category_totals(records)
totals.keys.sort.each do |c|
  puts "#{c} #{totals[c]}"
end
